messages:
olivia: heads up — customer 'acme' reported p99 token latency jumped ~3x at 03:12 UTC. graphs show a sharp step starting 03:10 which matches the canary we pushed. :frowning_face:

samir: ack. which canary exactly? was that the hw_map_priority tweak for better nvlink locality?

olivia: yes — the heuristic change that prefers SDPA on certain seq len combos. rollout started 03:05, canary group completed 03:09, global at 03:10.

nikhil: logs show a bunch of fallback events after 03:10: 
```
WARN kernel_selector: no flashopt candidate, falling back to generic_attention_kernel
metric=kernel_fallback count=178
```
looks like SDPA kernel selection misrouted a subset of requests to a non-optimized path.

jess: any correlation with model or tokenization? ACME uses long-chat profile (avg len ~1200).

olivia: yes, long sequences. the new heuristic had a bug where hw_map_priority bumped SDPA only if seq_len between 256-1024; for >1024 it skipped flashopt candidate selection and went generic.

cs-tier2: customer is complaining loudly, asked for ETA to fix and whether we can roll back. They see 700ms -> 2.4s p99.

samir: mitigation plan: 1) toggle heuristic back for global (flip rollback flag) 2) autoscale additional capacity for acme's project to reduce queueing 3) investigate compile flag interaction that made generic kernel slower after fallback.

olivia: i can flip the rollout flag now. who wants to own the toggle? oncall?

oncall-bot: deploy-flag rollback_hw_map_priority executed by olivia at 03:22 UTC — rollout started.

nikhil: after rollback, monitoring shows p99 trending down within 5 mins. looks much better at 03:28 (p99 ~820ms).

jess: good. we should still look at why generic path is so slow. can we repro locally? steps to repro: 
1) start model-serving container with compile flags: `RUNTIME_OPT_LEVEL=O2 KERNEL_FLAGS='-DDISABLE_FLASH_TUNING'`
2) send requests with seq_len 1400 using our loadgen: `python loadgen.py --seq 1400 --qps 20 --model acme-chat-v3`
3) tail `kernel_selector` logs

nikhil: repro confirmed in staging when we force fallback. noticed extra memcpy in kernel path: stack snippet: `memcpy -> cudaMemcpyAsync -> generic_attention_execute` which we don't see in flashopt.

samir: possible regressions: a) heuristic misselecting kernels for >1024 seqs b) compile-time flag change caused slower generic kernel c) recent CUDA driver on some nodes triggers fallback. we should triage all three but prioritize heuristic fix + quick kernel perf patch.

infra: also saw 12% of hosts in us-west-2 had older nvidia driver (470.x) vs fleet 515.x; scheduler might've routed some requests to those. could be compounding.

olivia: agreed. immediate actions: 
- rollback heuristic (done)
- narrow canary to only nodes with driver 515 until we validate (infra)
- patch kernel selector to treat >1024 seqs with flashopt candidate if model has cached KV support (samir/nikhil)
- open support note to ACME explaining rollback and expected impact (cs-tier2)

cs-tier2: i'll draft the note and ping legal for the SLA language. pls include the mitigation steps and ETA for a proper fix.

nikhil: i'll run focused benchmarks on generic vs flashopt for seq lengths 512/1024/1400 and paste numbers here. early numbers: flashopt p99 ~420ms, generic p99 ~1.9s for seq 1400 on A10.

jess: create an internal ticket referencing this thread and add perf artifacts + reproducer. recommend short-term hotfix: enable a fallback to flashopt single-threaded fallback kernel when generic path exceeds threshold latency.

samir: agree. also add a metric + alert: kernel_fallback.rate > 0.5% AND p99_delta > 30% => auto-roll flag and page eng-runtime oncall.

olivia: followups: 
- nik will own perf repro and kernel patch (PR target EOD)
- samir will own kernel_selector guard and metric/alert (PR target tomorrow)
- infra will pin driver-similar nodes for canaries (done)
- cs-tier2 will send customer update (in progress)

oncall-bot: incident created INC-2028-184123; priority=P2; assignees=[nikhil, samir, olivia].

olivia: thanks all. once PRs land we'll do a constrained canary on non-prod first, then small customer subset. tagging for postmortem: capture rollout gating test coverage for seq len edgecases. :memo:
